note: Hand draft 2026-11-02 (SG). Rodent antipsychotic screens predicted efficacy; engagement and dose translated, efficacy did not.

engagement.note: Papaverine raised striatal cGMP and cAMP and CREB/ERK phosphorylation in rats; effects absent in PDE10A knockouts.
[11C]T-773 PET: PDE10A occupancy in human putamen rose dose- and concentration-dependently (2.8-72.1% at 3-1000 mg TAK-063), as rat occupancy had.
engagement.short: Human PET occupancy tracks dose as in rat

dose.note: TP-10 gave antipsychotic-like effects in rodents at defined exposures; the dose rationale for clinical compounds came from rodent occupancy-efficacy.

In the monotherapy trial, 'pharmacokinetics exposures seemed adequate for binding/inhibiting PDE10A enzyme'; in the adjunctive trial exposures were 'within the range predicted to be adequate for demonstrating efficacy'.
dose.reason: Predicted exposure was reached in patients

efficacy.note: Papaverine inhibited conditioned avoidance and PCP/amphetamine hyperlocomotion in rats and mice: 'behavioral models predictive of antipsychotic activity'.

PF-02545920 monotherapy: neither dose beat placebo on PANSS while risperidone did; adjunctive trial also null. Authors: results 'refute the hypothesis that PDE10A inhibitors have use as antipsychotic agents'. TAK-063 (2018) also missed its primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: Three PDE10A inhibitors fail; risperidone works
efficacy.reason: Screens predicted efficacy; patients showed none

safety.note: TP-10 produced relatively low catalepsy in rats, read as predicting a low extrapyramidal risk in man.
Dystonia in 6/74 on PF-02545920 15 mg vs 3/74 placebo; TAK-063 trial reported akathisia and dystonia more frequent than placebo.

label: Schizophrenia (PDE10A)
